narrative: Material PL1__M115A2E8 exhibits erratic, high-volume demand with a CV of 0.526 and a statistically significant upward trend across the observation window. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.38) with occasional spikes to 5.1 days. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected to respond promptly to demand events while keeping order quantities economically efficient. Safety stock was set at 820 units (z=1.645) to achieve the 95% service level target, a significant increase from the current ERP value of 85 units which is critically inadequate.
warnings: SAP safety stock of 85 units is critically insufficient for 95% service level — recommend urgent update to 820 units.
Significant upward demand trend detected — reorder point and safety stock should be reviewed quarterly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The erratic demand pattern with high daily volumes and moderate lead-time variability makes continuous review preferable to periodic review, as it reacts promptly to consumption events. Fixed order quantity (EOQ-derived, MOQ-constrained) minimizes total ordering and holding costs. The upward trend further supports continuous monitoring over fixed-interval replenishment.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not currently binding (utilization at 63.6% of max_storage_units after replenishment). However, if the upward demand trend continues and safety stock is revised upward in future reviews, the 2234-unit ceiling may become relevant. Monitor quarterly.
